passages.text: Paul looked directly at the Sanhedrin and said, “Brothers, I have conducted myself before God in all good conscience to this day.”
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before the Sanhedrin.
The Sanhedrin was the Jewish council of leaders.
Paul looked directly at them.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Brothers, I have lived my life before God with a good conscience.
I have done this up to this very day.”
passages.original: Ἀτενίσας δὲ ὁ Παῦλος τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἶπεν Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ἐγὼ πάσῃ συνειδήσει ἀγαθῇ πεπολίτευμαι τῷ Θεῷ ἄχρι ταύτης τῆς ἡμέρας

passages.text: At this, the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.
passages.sermon:
The high priest was named Ananias.
Ananias gave an order.
He spoke to the people standing near Paul.
Ananias told them to strike Paul on the mouth.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἁνανίας ἐπέταξεν τοῖς παρεστῶσιν αὐτῷ τύπτειν αὐτοῦ τὸ στόμα

passages.text: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit here to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck.”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke directly to Ananias, the high priest.
Paul said, “God will strike you.”
Paul called Ananias a whitewashed wall.
Paul said, “You sit here to judge me by the law.”
Paul said, “But you break the law.”
Paul said, “You order them to strike me.”
passages.original: Τότε ὁ Παῦλος πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν Τύπτειν σε μέλλει ὁ Θεός τοῖχε κεκονιαμένε καὶ σὺ κάθῃ κρίνων με κατὰ τὸν νόμον καὶ παρανομῶν κελεύεις με τύπτεσθαι

passages.text: But those standing nearby said, “How dare you insult the high priest of God!”
passages.sermon:
Several people stood near Paul.
These people heard Paul speak.
They spoke to Paul.
They said, “You insult the high priest of God.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ παρεστῶτες εἶπαν Τὸν ἀρχιερέα τοῦ Θεοῦ λοιδορεῖς

passages.text: “Brothers,” Paul replied, “I was not aware that he was the high priest, for it is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the people.
He said, “Brothers, I did not know he was the high priest.”
Paul respected the law of God.
He explained, “It is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’”
passages.original: Ἔφη τε ὁ Παῦλος Οὐκ ᾔδειν ἀδελφοί ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀρχιερεύς γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Ἄρχοντα τοῦ λαοῦ σου οὐκ ἐρεῖς κακῶς

passages.text: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and others Pharisees, called out in the Sanhedrin, “Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. It is because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial.”
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before the Sanhedrin.
The Sanhedrin was the Jewish council.
Paul saw that some men in the council were Sadducees.
He saw that others were Pharisees.
Paul spoke loudly to the council.
He said, “Brothers, I am a Pharisee.
My father was also a Pharisee.
I am on trial because I hope in the resurrection of the dead.”
passages.original: Γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ὅτι τὸ ἓν μέρος ἐστὶν Σαδδουκαίων τὸ δὲ ἕτερον Φαρισαίων ἔκραζεν ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ἐγὼ Φαρισαῖός εἰμι υἱὸς Φαρισαίων περὶ ἐλπίδος καὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι

passages.text: As soon as he had said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the assembly.
He said he was a Pharisee.
He said he was on trial because of his hope in the resurrection of the dead.
The Pharisees and Sadducees heard him.
A dispute broke out between the Pharisees and the Sadducees.
The assembly became divided.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐγένετο στάσις τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων καὶ ἐσχίσθη τὸ πλῆθος

passages.text: For the Sadducees say that there is neither a resurrection, nor angels, nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.
passages.sermon:
The Sadducees are a group of Jewish leaders.
The Sadducees say there is no resurrection.
The Sadducees say there are no angels.
The Sadducees say there are no spirits.
The Pharisees are another group of Jewish leaders.
The Pharisees agree that there is a resurrection.
The Pharisees agree that there are angels.
The Pharisees agree that there are spirits.
passages.original: Σαδδουκαῖοι μὲν γὰρ λέγουσιν μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν μήτε ἄγγελον μήτε πνεῦμα Φαρισαῖοι δὲ ὁμολογοῦσιν τὰ ἀμφότερα

passages.text: A great clamor arose, and some scribes from the party of the Pharisees got up and contended sharply, “We find nothing wrong with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”
passages.sermon:
Some scribes belonged to the Pharisees.
The Pharisees believed in resurrection, angels, and spirits.
A great clamor arose among the people.
Some Pharisee scribes stood up.
They argued strongly.
They said, “We find nothing wrong with this man.”
They also said, “What if a spirit has spoken to him?”
They said, “What if an angel has spoken to him?”
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ κραυγὴ μεγάλη καὶ ἀναστάντες τινὲς τῶν γραμματέων τοῦ μέρους τῶν Φαρισαίων διεμάχοντο λέγοντες Οὐδὲν κακὸν εὑρίσκομεν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ εἰ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ ἢ ἄγγελος

passages.text: The dispute grew so violent that the commander was afraid they would tear Paul to pieces. He ordered the soldiers to go down and remove him by force and bring him into the barracks.
passages.sermon:
A violent dispute broke out.
The Roman commander saw the danger.
He feared that the crowd would tear Paul apart.
He gave an order to the soldiers.
He told them to go down to the crowd.
He told them to seize Paul by force.
He told them to take Paul away from the crowd.
He told them to bring Paul into the barracks.
passages.original: πολλῆς δὲ γινομένης στάσεως φοβηθεὶς ὁ χιλίαρχος μὴ διασπασθῇ ὁ Παῦλος ὑπ’ αὐτῶν ἐκέλευσεν τὸ στράτευμα καταβὰν ἁρπάσαι αὐτὸν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν ἄγειν τε εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν

passages.text: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, “Take courage! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord appeared to Paul the next night.
The Lord stood near Paul.
The Lord spoke to Paul.
The Lord said, “Take courage!”
The Lord said, “You have testified about Me in Jerusalem.”
The Lord said, “You must also testify about Me in Rome.”
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ νυκτὶ ἐπιστὰς αὐτῷ ὁ Κύριος εἶπεν Θάρσει ὡς γὰρ διεμαρτύρω τὰ περὶ ἐμοῦ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ οὕτω σε δεῖ καὶ εἰς Ῥώμην μαρτυρῆσαι

passages.text: When daylight came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
passages.sermon:
Daylight came.
The Jews formed a conspiracy.
They made a solemn oath.
They promised not to eat.
They promised not to drink.
They would keep this oath until they had killed Paul.
passages.original: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ποιήσαντες συστροφὴν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνεθεμάτισαν ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες μήτε φαγεῖν μήτε πιεῖν ἕως οὗ ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸν Παῦλον

passages.text: More than forty of them were involved in this plot.
passages.sermon:
More than forty men joined this plot.
These men planned together to kill Paul.
They acted as a group.
They shared the same purpose.
passages.original: ἦσαν δὲ πλείους τεσσεράκοντα οἱ ταύτην τὴν συνωμοσίαν ποιησάμενοι

passages.text: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.
passages.sermon:
More than forty Jews formed a plot against Paul.
They went to the chief priests and elders.
They spoke to the chief priests and elders.
They said, “We have made a solemn oath.
We will not eat anything.
We will not drink anything.
We will keep this oath until we have killed Paul.”
passages.original: οἵτινες προσελθόντες τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις εἶπαν Ἀναθέματι ἀνεθεματίσαμεν ἑαυτοὺς μηδενὸς γεύσασθαι ἕως οὗ ἀποκτείνωμεν τὸν Παῦλον

passages.text: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you on the pretext of examining his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him on the way.”
passages.sermon:
More than forty men made a plot to kill Paul.
They spoke to the chief priests and elders.
They said, “You and the Sanhedrin must ask the commander to bring Paul to you.
Tell the commander you want to examine Paul’s case more carefully.
We are ready to kill Paul before he arrives.”
passages.original: νῦν οὖν ὑμεῖς ἐμφανίσατε τῷ χιλιάρχῳ σὺν τῷ συνεδρίῳ ὅπως καταγάγῃ αὐτὸν εἰς ὑμᾶς ὡς μέλλοντας διαγινώσκειν ἀκριβέστερον τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς δὲ πρὸ τοῦ ἐγγίσαι αὐτὸν ἕτοιμοί ἐσμεν τοῦ ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν

passages.text: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner.
Paul had a sister.
Her son was Paul's nephew.
Some men made a plot to kill Paul.
Paul’s nephew heard about this plot.
He went to the barracks.
He told Paul about the plot.
passages.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀδελφῆς Παύλου τὴν ἐνέδραν παραγενόμενος καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ Παύλῳ

passages.text: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner.
Paul saw a young man.
Paul called one of the centurions.
Paul spoke to the centurion.
Paul said, “Take this young man to the commander.”
Paul said, “He has something to tell the commander.”
passages.original: προσκαλεσάμενος δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἕνα τῶν ἑκατονταρχῶν ἔφη Τὸν νεανίαν τοῦτον ἄπαγε πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον ἔχει γὰρ ἀπαγγεῖλαί τι αὐτῷ

passages.text: So the centurion took him to the commander and said, “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
passages.sermon:
A centurion took the young man.
He brought the young man to the commander.
The centurion spoke to the commander.
He said, “Paul is a prisoner.
Paul called me.
Paul asked me to bring this young man to you.
This young man has something to tell you.”
passages.original: Ὁ μὲν οὖν παραλαβὼν αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ φησίν Ὁ δέσμιος Παῦλος προσκαλεσάμενός με ἠρώτησεν τοῦτον τὸν νεανίσκον ἀγαγεῖν πρὸς σέ ἔχοντά τι λαλῆσαί σοι

passages.text: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked, “What do you need to tell me?”
passages.sermon:
The commander was a Roman officer in charge of many soldiers.
He took the young man by the hand.
He led the young man away from the others.
He spoke to the young man privately.
He asked the young man a question.
He said, “What do you need to tell me?”
passages.original: Ἐπιλαβόμενος δὲ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ χιλίαρχος καὶ ἀναχωρήσας κατ’ ἰδίαν ἐπυνθάνετο Τί ἐστιν ὃ ἔχεις ἀπαγγεῖλαί μοι

passages.text: He answered, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of acquiring more information about him.
passages.sermon:
The young man spoke to the commander.
He said the Jews have made a plan.
They will ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow.
They will pretend they want to learn more about Paul.
This is only a pretext.
Their real purpose is not to get information.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὅτι Οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι συνέθεντο τοῦ ἐρωτῆσαί σε ὅπως αὔριον τὸν Παῦλον καταγάγῃς εἰς τὸ συνέδριον ὡς μέλλον τι ἀκριβέστερον πυνθάνεσθαι περὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him; they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”
passages.sermon:
The young man warned the commander about a plot against Paul.
He said, “Do not let the Jews persuade you.”
More than forty men are waiting to ambush Paul.
These men have made a vow.
They promised not to eat or drink until they kill Paul.
They are ready now.
They are waiting for your consent.
passages.original: σὺ οὖν μὴ πεισθῇς αὐτοῖς ἐνεδρεύουσιν γὰρ αὐτὸν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες πλείους τεσσεράκοντα οἵτινες ἀνεθεμάτισαν ἑαυτοὺς μήτε φαγεῖν μήτε πιεῖν ἕως οὗ ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν καὶ νῦν εἰσιν ἕτοιμοι προσδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπὸ σοῦ ἐπαγγελίαν

passages.text: So the commander dismissed the young man and instructed him, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”
passages.sermon:
The commander was in charge of the soldiers.
The commander released the young man.
The commander gave the young man an order.
He said, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”
passages.original: Ὁ μὲν οὖν χιλίαρχος ἀπέλυσε τὸν νεανίσκον παραγγείλας Μηδενὶ ἐκλαλῆσαι ὅτι ταῦτα ἐνεφάνισας πρὸς ἐμέ

passages.text: Then he called two of his centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night.
passages.sermon:
The Roman commander acted quickly.
He called two of his centurions.
He gave them clear orders.
He said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers.”
He also said, “Prepare seventy horsemen.”
He added, “Prepare two hundred spearmen.”
He told them, “All of you must go to Caesarea.”
He said, “You must leave at the third hour of the night.”
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενός τινας δύο τῶν ἑκατονταρχῶν εἶπεν Ἑτοιμάσατε στρατιώτας διακοσίους ὅπως πορευθῶσιν ἕως Καισαρείας καὶ ἱππεῖς ἑβδομήκοντα καὶ δεξιολάβους διακοσίους ἀπὸ τρίτης ὥρας τῆς νυκτός

passages.text: Provide mounts for Paul to take him safely to Governor Felix.”
passages.sermon:
The commander spoke to his centurions.
He told them to provide animals.
They must give these animals to Paul.
Paul will ride on these animals.
They must take Paul safely.
They must bring Paul to Governor Felix.
passages.original: κτήνη τε παραστῆσαι ἵνα ἐπιβιβάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον διασώσωσι πρὸς Φήλικα τὸν ἡγεμόνα

passages.text: And he wrote the following letter: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.
passages.sermon:
Claudius Lysias was a Roman commander.
He wrote a letter.
He addressed the letter to Governor Felix.
He called Felix "His Excellency."
He greeted Felix in the letter.
passages.original: γράψας ἐπιστολὴν ἔχουσαν τὸν τύπον τοῦτον Κλαύδιος Λυσίας Τῷ κρατίστῳ ἡγεμόνι Φήλικι Χαίρειν

passages.text: This man was seized by the Jews, and they were about to kill him when I came with my troops to rescue him. For I had learned that he is a Roman citizen, and since I wanted to understand their charges against him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.
passages.sermon:
Claudius Lysias was a Roman commander.
The Jews seized this man named Paul.
They were about to kill Paul.
I came with my soldiers.
I rescued Paul from them.
I had learned that Paul is a Roman citizen.
I wanted to know why they accused him.
I brought Paul to their Sanhedrin, their council.
passages.original: Τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον συλλημφθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ μέλλοντα ἀναιρεῖσθαι ὑπ’ αὐτῶν ἐπιστὰς σὺν τῷ στρατεύματι ἐξειλάμην μαθὼν ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν βουλόμενός τε ἐπιγνῶναι τὴν αἰτίαν δι’ ἣν ἐνεκάλουν αὐτῷ κατήγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν

passages.text: I found that the accusation involved questions about their own law, but there was no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.
passages.sermon:
Claudius Lysias is a Roman commander.
He wrote a letter to Governor Felix about Paul.
Claudius Lysias found Paul accused by the Jews.
The accusation was about questions of the Jewish law.
Claudius Lysias found no charge against Paul that deserved death.
He found no charge against Paul that deserved imprisonment.
passages.original: ὃν εὗρον ἐγκαλούμενον περὶ ζητημάτων τοῦ νόμου αὐτῶν μηδὲν δὲ ἄξιον θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ἔχοντα ἔγκλημα

passages.text: When I was informed that there was a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also instructed his accusers to present their case against him before you.
passages.sermon:
I learned about a plot against this man.
I acted immediately.
I sent him to you at once.
I gave instructions to his accusers.
I told them to state their charges against him before you.
passages.original: Μηνυθείσης δέ μοι ἐπιβουλῆς εἰς τὸν ἄνδρα ἔσεσθαι ἐξαυτῆς ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ παραγγείλας καὶ τοῖς κατηγόροις λέγειν τὰ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπὶ σοῦ

passages.text: So the soldiers followed their orders and brought Paul by night to Antipatris.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers received orders.
The soldiers obeyed these orders.
The soldiers took Paul with them.
They traveled at night.
They brought Paul to Antipatris.
passages.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν στρατιῶται κατὰ τὸ διατεταγμένον αὐτοῖς ἀναλαβόντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον διὰ νυκτὸς εἰς τὴν Ἀντιπατρίδα

passages.text: The next day they returned to the barracks and let the horsemen go on with him.
passages.sermon: The soldiers guarded Paul during the night.\r\nThe next day, the soldiers returned to their barracks.\r\nThey allowed the horsemen to continue traveling with Paul.
passages.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἐάσαντες τοὺς ἱππεῖς ἀπέρχεσθαι σὺν αὐτῷ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν

passages.text: When the horsemen arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and presented Paul to him.
passages.sermon: The horsemen arrived in Caesarea.\r\nThey delivered the letter to the governor.\r\nThey presented Paul to the governor.
passages.original: οἵτινες εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν καὶ ἀναδόντες τὴν ἐπιστολὴν τῷ ἡγεμόνι παρέστησαν καὶ τὸν Παῦλον αὐτῷ

passages.text: The governor read the letter and asked what province Paul was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia, he said, “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.” Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s Praetorium.
passages.sermon:
The governor received the letter.
He read the letter.
He asked Paul, “What province are you from?”
Paul was from Cilicia.
The governor learned this.
He said to Paul, “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.”
He gave an order.
He ordered that Paul must be kept under guard.
He ordered that Paul must stay in Herod’s Praetorium.
passages.original: Ἀναγνοὺς δὲ καὶ ἐπερωτήσας ἐκ ποίας ἐπαρχείας ἐστὶν καὶ πυθόμενος ὅτι ἀπὸ Κιλικίας Διακούσομαί σου ἔφη Ὅταν καὶ οἱ κατήγοροί σου παραγένωνται κελεύσας ἐν τῷ πραιτωρίῳ τοῦ Ἡρῴδου φυλάσσεσθαι αὐτόν
